workflow.name: Track LinkedIn hiring signals with Bright Data, OpenAI, Airtable, HubSpot and Slack
workflow.description:
## How it works

- A daily Schedule Trigger pulls active LinkedIn job-search URLs from Airtable
- Bright Data Web Unlocker scrapes each search results page
- GPT extracts structured job data from the raw HTML
- A second GPT call scores each job as a HIGH / MEDIUM / LOW buying signal and drafts a personalized cold outreach email
- HIGH/MEDIUM signals are pushed to HubSpot as deals and notified to the sales team in Slack

## Set up steps

- Setup time: ~10 minutes
- Connect Airtable, Bright Data, OpenAI, HubSpot and Slack credentials
- Add LinkedIn job-search URLs to your Airtable with `Active = TRUE`
- Pick the Slack channel in the notification node
- Activate the workflow

See the sticky notes inside the workflow to swap Airtable, OpenAI, HubSpot or Slack for your preferred tools.

workflow.name: AI Hiring Signal Tracker powered by Bright Data

parameters.content:
# 🎯 AI Hiring Signal Tracker powered by Bright Data

Turn LinkedIn job postings into qualified pipeline. Detect when target companies are hiring sales/eng/leadership roles, score the signal with AI, draft personalized outreach, and sync to HubSpot + Slack.

## How it works

1. **Schedule Trigger** runs every morning
2. **Airtable** returns the active LinkedIn job-search URLs to monitor
3. **Bright Data Web Unlocker** scrapes each search results page
4. **GPT extracts** structured job data from the raw HTML (title, company, location, etc.)
5. **GPT scores** each job as a HIGH / MEDIUM / LOW buying signal and drafts a cold outreach email
6. **HubSpot** creates a deal for HIGH/MEDIUM signals
7. **Slack** alerts the sales team with the rationale and suggested email

## Why Bright Data?

- Scrapes LinkedIn search pages reliably (handles JS, anti-bot, geo)
- Returns clean Markdown ready for LLM parsing
- Scales from 1 to thousands of searches per day

## Prerequisites

- A [Bright Data](https://brightdata.com) account with a Web Unlocker zone
- An [OpenAI](https://platform.openai.com) API key
- An [Airtable](https://airtable.com) base with `Searches` table (`LinkedIn URL`, `Active`, `Last Run`)
- A [HubSpot](https://hubspot.com) account
- A [Slack](https://slack.com) workspace

## Setup (~10 min)

1. Connect Airtable, Bright Data, OpenAI, HubSpot and Slack credentials
2. Add LinkedIn job-search URLs to Airtable with `Active = TRUE`
3. Pick your Slack channel in the notification node
4. Activate the workflow

## 🚀 1. Trigger & Get Searches

The **Schedule Trigger** kicks off daily at 9am. **Airtable** returns the active LinkedIn search URLs (sorted by `Last Run` so the oldest gets refreshed first), and the **loop** processes them one by one.

### 🔄 Swap-friendly
- Trigger → Webhook, Cron, Form, Chat
- CRM → HubSpot, Notion, Sheets, Postgres…

## 🌐 2. Scrape & Parse Jobs

**Bright Data Web Unlocker** fetches the LinkedIn search page as clean Markdown. **GPT-5.4-mini** then extracts a structured list of up to 30 jobs (title, company, location, posted date, URL, early applicant flag…). The **JS code** safely parses the JSON, even when the model truncates its output.

- Bright Data handles JS, CAPTCHAs, geo-blocks
- The LLM does the structured parsing — no fragile CSS selectors
- 🔄 Swap GPT for any LLM (Claude, Gemini, Mistral, Groq…)

## 🧠 3. AI Signal Analysis

For each job, **GPT-4o-mini** returns:
- `signal_strength` (HIGH / MEDIUM / LOW)
- `rationale` (1 sentence)
- `outreach_email` (3-4 sentence draft)

Uses a strict JSON schema so the output is always valid.

🔄 Swap for any LLM.

## 🎯 4. Filter, Sync & Notify

1. **IF** keeps only HIGH or MEDIUM signals (LOW signals are skipped)
2. **HubSpot** creates a deal with the rationale and the suggested email
3. **Slack** alerts the sales team with the full context and the HubSpot deal link

### 🔄 Swap-friendly
- CRM → Salesforce, Pipedrive, Attio, Close, Notion…
- Channel → Email, Discord, Teams, Telegram, SMS…

values.content:
You are a LinkedIn job posting parser. Extract structured data from raw LinkedIn jobs HTML. Output ONLY valid JSON, no markdown, no preamble, no explanations. Format: { "jobs": [ { "title": "Account Executive", "company": "Acme Corp", "company_linkedin_slug": "acme-corp", "location": "San Francisco, CA", "posted_date": "2 hours ago", "posted_iso": "2026-05-05", "job_url": "https://www.linkedin.com/jobs/view/123456", "early_applicant": true, "actively_hiring": true } ] } Extract from
  • ...
    • blocks. - title:

    - company:

    ... - company_linkedin_slug: from the company link href, extract slug after /company/ - location: - posted_date: text inside - posted_iso: from - job_url: from - early_applicant: true if "Be an early applicant" appears in the card - actively_hiring: true if "Actively Hiring" appears in the card Limit to first 30 jobs. If no jobs found, return {"jobs": []}.

=Extract jobs from this LinkedIn HTML chunk:

{{ $json }}

You are a B2B sales buying signal analyzer + outreach copywriter.

Given a job posting, classify if it's a buying signal AND draft a personalized cold outreach email if relevant.

Output ONLY valid JSON with this exact structure:

{
  "signal_strength": "HIGH" | "MEDIUM" | "LOW",
  "rationale": "1 sentence explaining why",
  "outreach_email": "3-4 sentence cold email draft (only if HIGH or MEDIUM, otherwise empty string)"
}

HIGH signals: Senior leadership hire (Head of, VP, Founding role), multiple roles open at same company, net-new sales hire at B2B SaaS.

MEDIUM signals: Mid-level B2B sales/eng/marketing roles at growing companies.

LOW signals: Junior IC roles, sports teams, retail/hospitality, agency staffing, geographic-specific sales (Tampa AE, etc.). Set outreach_email to "" for LOW signals.

Email style: 3-4 sentences max. Reference the specific hiring signal. Soft CTA (book 15 min). No "I hope this finds you well". First-person from the rep.

additionalFields.dealName: =Hiring signal — {{ $('Parse JSON Output').item.json.jobs[0].company }} hiring {{ $('Parse JSON Output').item.json.jobs[0].title }}

data.details:
The IF node can be used to implement binary conditional logic in your workflow. You can set up one-to-many conditions to evaluate each item of data being inputted into the node. That data will either evaluate to TRUE or FALSE and route out of the node accordingly.

This node has multiple types of conditions: Bool, String, Number, and Date & Time.
